concept.name: Immutable Infrastructure

relationships.description: Connects Immutable Infrastructure to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Servers, containers, and OS images are never patched or reconfigured in place; every change triggers a fresh build, test, and atomic replacement of running instances.
spark.keyTakeaway: Replace, don't repair: baking artifacts once into versioned images eliminates configuration drift, snowflakes, and partial-upgrade outages.

concept.whyItMatters: Mutable fleets accumulate undocumented hotfixes, stale libraries, and divergent kernel states over months of SSH sessions and Ansible runs. Immutable infrastructure moves mutation to build time so production nodes are disposable, byte-identical replicas of a tested artifact.
whenToUse: Auto-scaling cloud fleets (AWS ASG, GCP MIG, Kubernetes) where nodes are frequently created and destroyed under load.
Regulated or security-sensitive environments requiring reproducible SBOMs, cryptographic image signing (Cosign/AMI), and 24-hour CVE rebuild SLAs.
Multi-region deployments where identical runtime behavior across US-East, EU-Central, and AP-South is mandatory.
whenNotToUse: Stateful single-node databases (PostgreSQL primary, bare-metal Ceph OSDs) where destroying the host risks petabyte-scale data movement.
Bare-metal or legacy on-prem hardware without PXE/iPXE automated provisioning or API-driven hypervisors.
Early-stage local prototyping where 10-minute Packer AMI bake cycles slow down tight edit-compile-debug loops.
keyPoints: Build-time mutation only: tools like Packer, Docker BuildKit, or Nix bake OS packages, binaries, and systemd units into a sealed artifact.
Read-only runtime filesystems: distributions like Bottlerocket and Talos Linux mount `/` as read-only SquashFS protected by dm-verity, blocking runtime tampering.
Instance metadata and env injection: immutable images stay environment-agnostic by reading secrets and config at boot via IMDSv2, Vault, or Kubernetes ConfigMaps.
Atomic traffic cutover: Blue/Green or Canary rollouts drain ALB/Envoy connections from old instances only after new instances pass `/healthz`.
Digest pinning over mutable tags: deploying `sha256:9f86d08...` instead of `:latest` guarantees that a scale-out event at 03:00 boots the exact same bits.

examples.title: AWS Golden AMI Pipeline with Packer & Terraform
examples.scenario: A fintech API running 80 EC2 `c6i.xlarge` instances needs an OpenSSL security patch across three AWS regions without downtime.
examples.outcome: CI runs `packer build` to produce a hardened Ubuntu 24.04 AMI (`ami-0a91f...`), verifies it with InSpec, updates the Terraform Launch Template, and triggers an ASG Instance Refresh (`MinHealthyPercentage=90`) that replaces all 80 nodes in 18 minutes with zero SSH access.

examples.title: Kubernetes Cluster Upgrade on Talos Linux
examples.scenario: Platform engineering must upgrade 45 bare-metal Kubernetes worker nodes from kernel 6.1 to 6.6 while keeping latency-sensitive gRPC workloads online.
examples.outcome: Because Talos has no SSH daemon or package manager, `talosctl upgrade` streams a signed SquashFS image to the inactive A/B boot partition, cordons and drains each node via PDBs, and reboots into the verified kernel in under 90 seconds per node.

tradeOffs.pro: Rollbacks take seconds by shifting load balancer targets back to the previous ASG or ReplicaSet.
tradeOffs.con: Small config or one-line script fixes require a full image build (3–15 minutes) instead of a 5-second `scp`.

tradeOffs.pro: Eliminates 'works on node-04' mysteries because every instance is derived from the exact same immutable hash.
tradeOffs.con: No SSH or package tools (`tcpdump`, `strace`) in production forces teams to invest in eBPF sidecars, ephemeral debug containers, and centralized logs.

tradeOffs.pro: Predictable artifact retention with clear lineage between Git commit SHA and running AMI/container digest.
tradeOffs.con: Daily base-image rebuilds across dozens of microservices generate terabytes of EBS snapshots and ECR layers requiring lifecycle pruning.

failureModes.name: Boot-Time Cloud-Init Drift
failureModes.description: Teams leave `apt-get update && apt-get install` inside `user_data` scripts; an upstream PyPI or Ubuntu mirror outage breaks auto-scaling at peak traffic.
failureModes.mitigation: Bake 100% of OS and application dependencies into the Packer/Docker image and restrict `user_data` to fast local wiring (env vars, hostname).

failureModes.name: Mutable Tag Hijacking (`:latest`)
failureModes.description: A scale-out event pulls `:prod` after a bad push, creating a split-brain fleet running two different binary versions under the same tag.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce immutable image tags and SHA-256 digests in Kubernetes admission controllers (Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper) and Terraform.

failureModes.name: Slow Image Pulls During Traffic Spikes
failureModes.description: Bloated 4 GB container images cause `ImagePullBackOff` or 5-minute cold starts when HPA scales from 10 to 100 pods.
failureModes.mitigation: Use multi-stage distroless builds (<100 MB), pre-warm EBS snapshots (AWS Fast Snapshot Restore), or enable eStargz lazy-pulling.

failureModes.name: Stateful Data Loss on Instance Termination
failureModes.description: An engineer stores local upload caches or SQLite files on instance ephemeral NVMe; an ASG replacement silently wipes customer data.
failureModes.mitigation: Externalize all state to RDS, S3, or detached EBS/PVCs with `Retain` reclaim policies and mount root filesystems read-only.

commonMistakes: Leaving SSH port 22 open 'just in case', which inevitably tempts engineers to apply undocumented hotfixes during incidents.
Hardcoding environment-specific secrets or database URLs inside the baked image instead of injecting them at runtime.
Forgetting to configure graceful connection draining (`deregistration_delay` / `preStop` sleep), causing 502 errors during instance replacement.
Skipping automated smoke tests against the newly baked AMI before promoting its ID to production Terraform state.
Never garbage-collecting old AMIs and container layers, leading to silent AWS snapshot quota exhaustion.

sections.content:
## The idea

Traditional server management treats machines like pets: you provision an OS once, then run Chef, Puppet, or Ansible repeatedly over months to mutate packages, sysctl flags, and binaries in place. Every failed run, manual hotfix, or skipped reboot leaves behind subtle state differences—configuration drift.

Immutable infrastructure treats compute instances like cattle by splitting the lifecycle into two strict phases. In the **build phase**, a pipeline starts from a clean base, installs dependencies, compiles or copies the application, runs security scans, and seals the result into a read-only artifact (an AWS AMI, GCP Image, or OCI container digest). In the **runtime phase**, instances boot from that artifact, fetch only environment-specific configuration (via IMDS, Vault, or Kubernetes Secrets), and never accept in-place mutations. When a CVE drops or code changes, you build a new artifact, spin up fresh instances, verify health, shift traffic, and terminate the old fleet.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider releasing `checkout-api` v2.14.0 on AWS EC2:

1. **Bake & Sign**: GitHub Actions triggers `packer build` from `ubuntu-24.04-minimal`. Packer installs the compiled Go binary, configures `systemd`, applies CIS Level 1 `sysctl` hardening, removes `openssh-server`, and outputs `ami-08f3c1e2a94b7d112`.
2. **Provision**: Terraform updates `aws_launch_template.checkout` with the new AMI ID and runs `aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh` with `InstanceWarmup=120` and `MinHealthyPercentage=90`.
3. **Verify & Drain**: New instances boot, read `DB_HOST` and TLS certs from AWS Secrets Manager, and pass `GET /healthz` on port 8080. Once the ALB marks a new target healthy, it shifts traffic and sends `SIGTERM` to an old instance, waiting 30 seconds (`deregistration_delay`) for in-flight HTTP/2 requests to finish before terminating it.
4. **Rollback**: If p99 latency spikes from 40 ms to 300 ms, Terraform or the ASG reverts the Launch Template to `ami-04d2a991c...`—no reverse-Ansible playbooks required.

sections.content:
## Separating artifact from configuration

An image is only reusable across `dev`, `staging`, and `prod` if environment-specific state is decoupled from the baked bits. Follow the Twelve-Factor config boundary:

- **Baked into the image**: OS kernel, libc/musl, runtime (JVM/Go/Python), application binary, static assets, default `systemd` or entrypoint scripts, and CA trust store.
- **Injected at boot**: Database endpoints, feature flag keys, TLS leaf certificates, and region identifiers via AWS IMDSv2, GCP Metadata Server, Vault Agent, or Kubernetes CSI Secrets Store.

If you bake a staging config file into the image, you break artifact promotion: the bits you tested in staging are no longer the bits you run in production.

## Mutable vs. immutable operating models

| Dimension | Mutable (Ansible / SSH) | Immutable VMs (Packer + ASG) | Immutable Containers (OCI + K8s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Patching mechanism** | `apt upgrade` in-place on live hosts | Rebuild AMI, rolling ASG replacement | Rebuild distroless image, `RollingUpdate` |
| **Rollback speed** | Slow, error-prone reverse playbooks | 2–5 min (revert Launch Template) | 10–30 sec (`kubectl rollout undo`) |
| **Configuration drift** | High; accumulates over months | Zero; identical EBS snapshot | Zero; read-only overlayfs + digest pin |
| **Cold-start overhead** | N/A (always warm) | 60–180 sec (EBS lazy load / Fast Snapshot) | 1–10 sec (cached layers on node) |
| **Best fit** | Legacy monoliths, stateful DB primaries | PCI/HIPAA VMs, GPU inference nodes | Stateless microservices, batch workers |

## Failure modes

- **Slow EBS snapshot hydration**: AWS lazily loads EBS blocks from S3 on first read, causing 10x latency spikes on freshly booted instances. Fix by enabling AWS EBS Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) or warming critical binaries in `/healthz`.
- **Broken `PreStop` / draining**: Terminating a pod or EC2 instance immediately on `SIGTERM` drops active keep-alive connections, producing HTTP 502s at the ALB. Fix with a 15–30s `preStop` sleep so kube-proxy/ALB endpoint removal propagates before the process exits.
- **Secret rotation deadlocks**: If secrets are only read once at boot, rotating a database password requires replacing the entire fleet. Use dynamic secret leases (Vault Agent or AWS Secrets Manager rotation + `SIGHUP` reload).

sections.eyebrow: 06 / Read-only root filesystems and runtime hardening
sections.content:
## Read-only root filesystems and runtime hardening

True immutability extends into the running OS. In Kubernetes, set `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, mounting `emptyDir` only for `/tmp` or `/var/run` with strict `sizeLimit` bounds. At the host OS layer, purpose-built Linux distributions like **AWS Bottlerocket** and **Talos Linux** eliminate shells, `ssh`, and package managers entirely, verifying every block read from the root partition against a cryptographic Merkle tree (`dm-verity`). If an attacker exploits an RCE vulnerability, they cannot drop a persistent binary or modify `/etc/passwd`.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Disable SSH (`sshd`) and remove package managers (`apt`, `yum`, `apk`) in production images.
- [ ] Pin every base image and deployment artifact by immutable `sha256` digest or signed AMI ID, never `:latest`.
- [ ] Enforce `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` on all stateless containers and isolate scratch space to bounded `emptyDir` mounts.
- [ ] Configure graceful connection draining (`deregistration_delay` >= 30s and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` >= 45s) on all load-balanced targets.
- [ ] Automate nightly base-image rebuilds with Trivy/Grype CVE gating and retention policies for old snapshots.

interviewProblems.title: Immutable Infrastructure
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Immutable Infrastructure. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Servers, containers, and OS images are never patched or reconfigured in place; every change triggers a fresh build, test, and atomic replacement of running instances.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Fleet Orchestrator applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Ingress & Health.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Ingress & Health experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Bake 100% of OS and application dependencies into the Packer/Docker image and restrict `user_data` to fast local wiring (env vars, hostname).

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Replace, don't repair: baking artifacts once into versioned images eliminates configuration drift, snowflakes, and partial-upgrade outages.
Avoid trap: Leaving SSH port 22 open 'just in case', which inevitably tempts engineers to apply undocumented hotfixes during incidents.
Avoid trap: Hardcoding environment-specific secrets or database URLs inside the baked image instead of injecting them at runtime.
When to reach for it: Auto-scaling cloud fleets (AWS ASG, GCP MIG, Kubernetes) where nodes are frequently created and destroyed under load.
When to reach for it: Regulated or security-sensitive environments requiring reproducible SBOMs, cryptographic image signing (Cosign/AMI), and 24-hour CVE rebuild SLAs.

putItTogether.title: Putting Immutable Infrastructure Together
putItTogether.summary: Replace, don't repair: baking artifacts once into versioned images eliminates configuration drift, snowflakes, and partial-upgrade outages.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Immutable Infrastructure before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: CI runs `packer build` to produce a hardened Ubuntu 24.04 AMI (`ami-0a91f...`), verifies it with InSpec, updates the Terraform Launch Template, and triggers an ASG Instance Refresh (`MinHealthyPercentage=90`) that replaces all 80 nodes in 18 minutes with zero SSH access.
